title: Future Forms: will / going to / Present Continuous
grammarTitle: Three Ways to Talk About the Future
grammarNote: В английском языке есть три основные формы для выражения будущего, и у каждой своё значение. WILL — для спонтанных решений, обещаний и предсказаний. GOING TO — для планов, уже принятых решений и предсказаний на основе доказательств. PRESENT CONTINUOUS — для конкретных договорённостей с датой и временем.

grammarTable.subject: will
grammarTable.example: "I'll help you." (решение прямо сейчас) / "It will be warm tomorrow." (предсказание)

grammarTable.subject: going to
grammarTable.example: "I'm going to visit Almaty." (уже запланировано) / "Look — it's going to rain!" (доказательство)

grammarTable.subject: Present Continuous
grammarTable.example: "I'm flying to Almaty on Friday." (конкретная дата, куплены билеты)

grammarTable.subject: will vs going to
grammarTable.example: "I'll have the pasta." (just decided) vs "I'm going to have pasta." (decided before)

grammarTable.subject: going to vs Pres. Cont.
grammarTable.example: "I'm going to visit." (plan) vs "I'm visiting on Monday." (confirmed, with time)

rows.example: "I'll carry your bag for you." (decided at the moment of speaking) ✅
"I'll call you when I arrive." / "I promise I won't be late." ✅
"I think it will rain tomorrow." / "You'll love Almaty — it's beautiful." ✅
"I'll get the tickets." / "Shall I help you with that?" ✅
✗ "I will visit Almaty next week." (if tickets already booked) → ✅ "I'm visiting Almaty next week."

grammarExtra.title: GOING TO — when to use it

rows.example: "I'm going to apply for the scholarship." (already decided) ✅
"Look at those clouds — it's going to rain!" (evidence = dark clouds) ✅
"I'm going to visit Georgia this summer." (plan made earlier) ✅
✗ "I'm going to help you." (at that moment, spontaneously) → ✅ "I'll help you."

grammarExtra.title: Present Continuous for future — when to use it

rows.example: "I'm meeting Zhibek at the airport on Friday." (confirmed, time set) ✅
"She's flying to Istanbul next Monday at 07:30." ✅
"I'm going to a conference." (plan) vs "I'm attending a conference on Thursday." (confirmed)
✗ "It's raining tomorrow." → ✅ "It's going to rain." or "It will rain."
Spontaneous — just decided now, in this conversation. ✅

rows.form: GOING TO: "I'm going to book a hostel."
rows.example: Plan made earlier — already decided before this conversation. ✅

rows.form: PRES. CONT.: "I'm booking a hostel on Thursday."
rows.example: Confirmed arrangement — date/time set, probably already arranged. ✅
Fixed schedule — timetable, not personal plan. ✅

grammarTip:
Три формы будущего — запомни разницу:

WILL → спонтанное решение / обещание / общее предсказание:
"I'll help you!" (только что решил)
"It will be warm." (моё предсказание)

GOING TO → уже принятый план / предсказание по доказательствам:
"I'm going to visit Georgia." (план уже есть)
"Look — it's going to rain!" (вижу тучи)

PRESENT CONTINUOUS → конкретная договорённость с датой:
"I'm flying to Almaty on Friday." (билеты куплены)
"We're meeting at 3." (договорились)

PRESENT SIMPLE → официальное расписание:
"The flight departs at 10:15." (расписание)

exercises.text: "Oh no, you dropped your bag! ___  help you pick it up."
exercises.hint: Spontaneous decision at the moment = WILL. "I'LL help you." ✅ (Not going to — going to = plan made before)

exercises.text: Kamila bought plane tickets last week. "She ___ fly to Almaty on Friday."
exercises.hint: Specific confirmed arrangement with a date (Friday) = PRESENT CONTINUOUS. "She IS FLYING to Almaty on Friday." ✅
Prediction based on visible evidence (dark clouds) = GOING TO. "It IS GOING TO RAIN!" ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form for a schedule.
exercises.hint: Official transport schedule = PRESENT SIMPLE. "The train LEAVES at 08:30." ✅ (Fixed timetable, not personal plan)

exercises.text: Rustam has been thinking about learning to drive for months. "___ get my driving licence this year."
exercises.hint: Pre-made intention (decided before this moment) = GOING TO. "I'M GOING TO get my licence." ✅

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses Present Continuous correctly for future?
exercises.text: Choose the sentence with a confirmed arrangement.
opts: "I'm meeting Zhibek at the airport on Sunday."
exercises.correct: "I'm meeting Zhibek at the airport on Sunday."
exercises.hint: "I'M MEETING Zhibek... on Sunday." = confirmed arrangement with specific day. ✅ NOT "it's raining" — weather ≠ confirmed arrangement.

exercises.text: "I've decided — ___ (apply) for a student internship in Astana next year."
exercises.hint: Decision made BEFORE this conversation = GOING TO. "I'M GOING TO APPLY." ✅

exercises.text: "A: What are you doing tomorrow? B: ___ visiting the Charyn Canyon with my friends."
exercises.hint: "I'M visiting the Charyn Canyon." = Present Continuous for confirmed future arrangement with friends. ✅

exercises.text: "I will to fly to Almaty next week." — What is wrong?
opts: "will" never takes "to" — should be "I will fly"
exercises.correct: "will" never takes "to" — should be "I will fly"
exercises.hint: ✗ "will TO fly" — NEVER! "will" + BASE FORM (no "to"). "I WILL FLY to Almaty." ✅

exercises.text: "You look tired. ___ (make) you a cup of tea?"
exercises.hint: "Shall I...?" = polite offer using will form. "SHALL I make you tea?" ✅ (Also: "I'll make you tea." ✅)

exercises.text: "I'm going to help you" can describe a spontaneous decision made right now.
exercises.hint: ✗ Spontaneous = WILL. "I'LL help you." ✅ "Going to" = pre-made intention. You cannot use going to for a spontaneous moment decision.

exercises.text: "I ___ probably be late — there's a lot of traffic." (prediction)
exercises.hint: "I'LL probably be late." = WILL for personal prediction. ✅ "Probably" + will is a common combination for uncertain predictions.

opts: It's a spontaneous decision made right now
questions.correct: It's a spontaneous decision made right now

questions.text: "I'm going to visit Georgia." — "going to" because:
questions.hint: "going to" = pre-made intention, decided before the moment of speaking. ✅

questions.text: "I'm flying to Almaty on Friday." — Present Continuous here means:
questions.hint: Present Continuous for future = confirmed arrangement. Specific day (Friday) + arranged. ✅

questions.text: "The train leaves at 08:30." — Present Simple here expresses:
questions.hint: Present Simple for timetables/schedules. "The train LEAVES at 08:30." = fixed timetable. ✅
Visible evidence (clouds) → GOING TO. "It IS GOING TO RAIN!" ✅

questions.text: "I will to fly to Almaty." — What is wrong?
opts: "will" + "to" is never correct — should be "will fly"
questions.correct: "will" + "to" is never correct — should be "will fly"
questions.hint: "will" + BASE FORM (no "to"). "I WILL FLY to Almaty." ✅ Never "will to fly"!

questions.text: Which is most natural for a spontaneous offer?
questions.hint: "I'LL carry your bag." = spontaneous offer, decided right now. WILL = ✅

questions.text: "She's meeting Amir at 3 p.m." — This is:
questions.hint: Present Continuous for future with specific time (3 p.m.) = confirmed arrangement. ✅

questions.text: "It will be warm in Almaty." — This is a:
questions.hint: "will" for prediction based on opinion or general expectation. "It WILL BE warm." ✅
Pre-made decision = GOING TO. "I'M GOING TO STUDY abroad next year." ✅

questions.text: Which sentence describes a confirmed arrangement with a date?
questions.hint: "I'm visiting on Saturday." = Present Continuous with specific day = confirmed arrangement. ✅

questions.text: "I probably won't be on time." — "Won't" is:
questions.hint: "WON'T" = will not. Irregular contraction. "I WON'T be on time." ✅ (Never "willn't"!)

questions.text: "Shall I book the tickets?" — This uses "shall" for:
questions.hint: "Shall I...?" = polite offer/suggestion (British English). Equivalent to "Do you want me to...?" ✅

questions.text: Compare: "I'm going to fly." vs "I'm flying on Thursday." — Difference?
opts: "Going to" = intention; "flying on Thursday" = confirmed with date
questions.correct: "Going to" = intention; "flying on Thursday" = confirmed with date
questions.hint: "going to fly" = plan/intention. "flying on Thursday" = confirmed arrangement with specific time. ✅

questions.text: "A: What are your plans? B: ___ (travel / going to) to Shymkent in July."
questions.hint: Pre-made plan = GOING TO. "I'M GOING TO TRAVEL to Shymkent in July." ✅

questions.text: Which uses Present Simple correctly for future?
questions.hint: Present Simple for fixed transport schedules: "The bus DEPARTS at 9." ✅ Timetables use Present Simple.
